_meta.indication: ODOMZO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced basal cell carcinoma (BCC) that has recurred following surgery or radiation therapy, or those who are not candidates for surgery or radiation therapy.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study CLDE225A2201 (A2201), a phase II study of two dose levels of sonidegib (LDE225) in locally advanced or metastatic basal cell carcinoma
pivotal_trials.design: Single, multicenter, double-blind, multiple cohort trial; patients randomized (2:1) to ODOMZO 800 mg or 200 mg orally once daily until disease progression or intolerable toxicity
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with locally advanced basal cell carcinoma (laBCC) or metastatic basal cell carcinoma (mBCC); the efficacy population was the 66 patients with laBCC randomized to 200 mg daily
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (ORR) by blinded central review (mRECIST for laBCC, RECIST v1.1 for mBCC); duration of response was a key secondary outcome
pivotal_trials.n: 230 patients enrolled (151 to 800 mg, 79 to 200 mg); 66 laBCC patients in the 200 mg efficacy analysis
pivotal_trials.result: In laBCC patients on 200 mg, ORR was 58% (95% CI: 45, 70), with 3 (5%) complete responses and 35 (53%) partial responses among 66 patients; median duration of response not reached

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) are muscle spasms (54%), alopecia (53%), dysgeusia (46%), fatigue (41%), nausea (39%), and musculoskeletal pain (32%). Musculoskeletal reactions occurred in 68% (54/79). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 18% of patients; most serious risks are rhabdomyolysis and embryofetal toxicity.
target_moa: Sonidegib is a Hedgehog pathway inhibitor that binds to and inhibits Smoothened (SMO), a transmembrane protein involved in Hedgehog signal transduction
modality: Small molecule (oral Smoothened antagonist / Hedgehog pathway inhibitor)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — ODOMZO can cause embryo-fetal death or severe birth defects when administered to a pregnant woman and is embryotoxic, fetotoxic, and teratogenic in animals; verify pregnancy status prior to initiating therapy and advise effective contraception.

rems.type: A REMS is not required to ensure safe and effective use of this drug; risks of teratogenicity and musculoskeletal toxicity can be mitigated through product labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Division did not refer the NDA to ODAC because the drug is not first in its class and the safety profile was acceptable for the indicated population.

summary.text: ODOMZO (sonidegib) is a new molecular entity approved under a standard-review NDA on the basis of a single trial (Study A2201) demonstrating durable objective responses (ORR 58%) in patients with locally advanced BCC; it was the second Hedgehog pathway inhibitor approved for this indication. No advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required; the approval carried five postmarketing requirements including carcinogenicity studies and a pregnancy pharmacovigilance study.

Sonidegib is an inhibitor of the Hedgehog pathway and is the second drug in this class to be considered for this indication.

Approval was based on demonstration of independently confirmed, durable objective responses in the subgroup of patients with laBCC. The ORR was 58% (95% confidence interval: 45, 70), consisting of 3 (5%) complete responses and 35 (53%) partial responses among the 66 patients with laBCC randomized to receive sonidegib 200 mg daily.
